answer: To resist sybil attacks each agent must lock a sparrow-sized bond of tokens while publishing a unique ferrous hardware root-of-trust that is mirrored into a public append-only log. Verifiers check that the mirror entry is fresh and unshared. An attacker creating N identities pays N times the hardware acquisition cost plus N bonds which are forfeited on any detected collision. This makes mass identity farming economically prohibitive without proportional real-world outlay.
